definition_zh: 欠（钱）；归功于；应给予；理应
definition_en: to have money still to pay, to be grateful to someone or something for a result, or to be under an obligation to give something
core_image: 账本上一行没有划掉的数字，提醒你还欠着别人
scene: 月底的餐桌上，一张写满数字的账单被推到对方面前。I still owe you two hundred yuan for the tickets.
sceneCN: 这里 owe 是「欠钱」（第 1 个义项：还欠着钱没付）；句意为我还欠你买票的两百块钱。图中可辨识物件：账单、餐盘、被推到桌对面的手势。

derivatives.zh: 由 owe 加 -ing 构成，表示「欠着的、尚未支付的」，常见于 owing to 表示「由于」
owe 的过去式与过去分词，表示已经欠下、曾被欠

senses.title: To have a debt to pay
senses.definition: to have borrowed money or goods and not yet paid for them
senses.definitionCN: 借了钱或拿了东西，还没有付清
senses.example: I still owe the shop twenty pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 我还欠那家店二十英镑。
senses.why: The Old English verb āgan meant to possess; a debt is what another person still holds a claim on, so the word came to name the part not yet handed over.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 āgan 本义是拥有；债务正是别人仍握有权利的那部分，于是这个词转指你还没交还出去的东西。

senses.title: To be grateful for a result
senses.definition: to be grateful to a person or thing because they made a good result possible
senses.definitionCN: 因为某人或某物促成了好结果而感激他
senses.example: She owes her career to a teacher who believed in her.
senses.exampleCN: 她把事业归功于一位相信她的老师。
senses.why: If a person still holds what you received, the debt can be a debt of gratitude; the ledger moves from money to credit for a result.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个人仍握着你得到的好处，这份债就成了感激之债；账本从金钱转成了对某份成果的功劳记录。

senses.title: To be under an obligation to give
senses.definition: to be obliged to give someone something such as an apology, an explanation or attention
senses.definitionCN: 有义务给某人某样东西，如道歉、解释或关注
senses.example: You owe him an explanation for leaving so suddenly.
senses.exampleCN: 你突然离开，欠他一个解释。
senses.why: A debt need not be money: any unfinished obligation, from an apology to a phone call, sits in the same place on the ledger.
senses.whyCN: 债不一定是钱：任何没完成的义务，从一句道歉到一个电话，都记在账本的同一栏。

senses.title: To be morally required to do something
senses.definition: in the phrase owe it to someone, to be morally required to do something for that person, especially for oneself
senses.definitionCN: 在 owe it to someone 这一说法里，指道义上应该为某人做某事，尤其应为自己的利益去做
senses.example: You owe it to yourself to take a real holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 你理应给自己放一个真正意义上的假。
senses.why: The same ledger can record a duty owed to oneself, which is why the phrase turns a moral claim into a kind of unpaid account.
senses.whyCN: 同一本账也能记下一个人对自己的责任，所以这个说法把道义要求写成了一笔尚未付清的账。

intro.en: Owe goes back to Old English āgan, to have or to possess; its modern meaning of debt grew out of the idea of something still held by another party.
intro.cn: owe 源自表示「拥有、持有」的古英语 āgan；今天「欠」的意思，是从「东西仍被另一方握有」这一观念长出来的。

items.en: The verb āgan meant to own, to have and to hold; a person could āgan land, cattle or money.
items.cn: 动词 āgan 意为拥有、持有；人可以拥有土地、牲畜或钱财。

items.en: A past form āhte began to take the sense of having a claim upon someone, and this is the seed of the debt sense.
items.cn: 过去式 āhte 开始带有「对某人拥有权利」的意思，这就是债务义的种子。

items.en: Middle English owen already meant both to possess and to be obliged to pay, depending on the sentence.
items.cn: 中古英语的 owen 已同时表示「拥有」与「有义务支付」，要看句子而定。

items.en: As own took over the plain sense of possession, owe was left with debt and obligation, and the split became permanent.
items.cn: 随着 own 接掌了纯粹的「拥有」义，owe 只剩下债务与义务，这一分工最终固定下来。

items.en: Modern English keeps owed and owing, and the phrase owing to, where a debt becomes the reason for something.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 owed 与 owing，以及 owing to，在那里一笔债变成了某事的原因。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the old verb of holding and its surviving relatives; the near-meaning group follows debt, gratitude and its opposite, repayment.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「持有」的旧动词及仍在使用的亲属词展开；近义组沿着债务、感激以及它的另一面——偿还——展开。

entries.definition: To possess something as property; the two words split from the same Old English verb.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物；这两个词由同一个古英语动词分出。

entries.definition: The old past tense of owe, now a modal verb for duty.
entries.definitionCN: owe 历史上的过去式，今为表示义务的情态动词。

entries.definition: Still unpaid, or, in owing to, because of.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未支付的；在 owing to 中表示「由于」。

entries.definition: Owing money, or grateful for help received.
entries.definitionCN: 负债的；受恩的。

entries.definition: To say that something is caused by a particular person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事归因于某人或某物。

entries.definition: To give someone praise for an achievement.
entries.definitionCN: 把成就归功于某人。

entries.definition: To pay back money that was borrowed.
entries.definitionCN: 偿还借来的钱。

normalIntro.en: The word is an old verb of holding whose debt sense survived while own took the plain sense of possession.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词原本是表示「持有」的旧动词，债务义留了下来，而纯粹的「拥有」义交给了 own。

normal.en: The Old English verb meant to have; a debt is what another person still has over you.
normal.cn: 古英语动词本义是持有；债务就是别人仍对你持有的一份东西。

normal.en: Own and owe split from the same verb: own keeps the possession, owe keeps the obligation.
normal.cn: own 与 owe 由同一个动词分出：own 留下拥有，owe 留下义务。

normal.en: Owing to works like a note on a receipt: one thing is charged to the account of another.
normal.cn: owing to 像收据上的备注：一件事被记到另一件事的账上。

normal.en: Ought is the old past tense of owe, which is why both still deal with duty.
normal.cn: ought 是 owe 旧的过去式，所以两者至今都在谈「应当」。

normal.en: You can owe an apology as easily as money; both are entries not yet settled.
normal.cn: 道歉和钱一样可以欠；两者都是还没结清的一笔。

abstract.en: A debt is a thread that keeps two people connected until it is paid.
abstract.cn: 债是一根线，在付清之前把两个人连着。

abstract.en: Gratitude is a ledger with no money in it, only names.
abstract.cn: 感激是一本没有钱数、只有名字的账。

abstract.en: To owe is to admit that part of what you are came from somewhere else.
abstract.cn: 欠，就是承认你之所以成为现在的样子，有一部分来自别处。

examples.en: I still owe the shop twenty pounds.
examples.cn: 我还欠那家店二十英镑。

examples.en: She owes her career to a teacher who believed in her.
examples.cn: 她把事业归功于一位相信她的老师。

examples.en: You owe him an explanation for leaving so suddenly.
examples.cn: 你突然离开，欠他一个解释。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧」——欠债的人看到账单只会喊一声「欧」，记住 owe 是欠。

root: 古英语 āgan（拥有、持有）到中古英语 owen；拥有义后来交给 own，owe 专指欠与归功于。同族词还有 ought、owing。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an unsettled claim; the senses spread from money to gratitude, to social obligations, and finally to duties owed to oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一笔没结清的权利；义项从金钱扩展到感激、社交义务，最后落到对自己也欠着一份责任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line in a notebook that has not been crossed out.
core.cn: 核心意象：本子上那一行始终没有划掉的记录。

branches.en: a shopkeeper's notebook with an unpaid line
branches.cn: 店主本子上没划掉的一行

branches.en: a teacher named in a speech of thanks
branches.cn: 致谢演讲里被点名的老师

branches.en: an unsent apology waiting on a phone screen
branches.cn: 手机屏幕上一条没发出的道歉

branches.en: a tired worker finally booking a holiday
branches.cn: 疲惫的职员终于订下了假期

branches.en: a debt to another person and a debt to oneself
branches.cn: 欠别人的一笔，欠自己的一笔

intro.en: The forms come from one Old English verb of holding, with an old past tense that survives as a modal verb and an -ing form that still marks an unpaid sum.
intro.cn: 这些形式都出自同一个表示「持有」的古英语动词，其中一个旧过去式作为情态动词留存，一个 -ing 形式仍表示未付的款项。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; it descends from an Old English verb of holding.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它出自一个表示「持有」的古英语动词。

items.meaningCN: owe 的过去式与过去分词

items.meaning: should, from the old past of owe
items.meaningCN: 应当，源自 owe 的旧过去式

definition_zh: 阉公牛；耕牛；牛（通称）
definition_en: a castrated adult male bovine used for draught; a bovine animal in compounds
core_image: 两头阉公牛并排套在木轭上，肩背隆起，拉着犁在硬土里前进
scene: 两头阉公牛并排套进木轭，肩峰顶住横木，犁铧在硬土里翻出连续的土块。The ox team pulled the plough to the field's far edge.
sceneCN: 这里指「套轭耕田的阉公牛」（第 1 个义项：役用阉公牛）；句意为这对耕牛把犁拉到田的最远端。

derivatives.zh: ox + -en（古英语复数词尾）→ 阉公牛的复数（语义偏移：保留强变化复数）
ox + herd（牧人）→ 牧牛人
ox + cart（车）→ 牛车
ox + bow（弯木）→ 牛轭弯木；河曲（语义偏移：指形似牛轭的河湾）
ox + hide（皮）→ 牛皮
ox + eye（眼）→ 牛眼菊（语义偏移：指花盘像牛眼的花）
ox + blood（血）→ 深红色（语义偏移：指像牛血的颜色）

senses.title: A castrated adult male bovine
senses.definition: an adult male bovine that has been castrated, usually for work
senses.definitionCN: 已阉割的成年公牛，通常用于劳作
senses.example: The ox was quieter than the bull beside it.
senses.exampleCN: 这头阉牛比旁边的公牛安静。
senses.why: The core sense is a sex-and-work class, not simply a male bovine.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个性别与劳作等级，而非单纯的雄性牛。

senses.title: A draught animal in a team
senses.definition: an ox trained to pull a plough, cart or load, usually paired with another
senses.definitionCN: 受训拉犁、拉车或拉货的牛，通常与另一头配对
senses.example: The team of oxen turned the heavy soil in long lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这对耕牛拉着长线翻动重土。
senses.why: Castration made the animal tractable, so work is the reason the class exists.
senses.whyCN: 阉割使动物温顺，因此劳作是这个等级存在的理由。

senses.title: A bovine in compounds
senses.definition: a general bovine reference in compounds such as oxhide, ox tongue or ox-eye
senses.definitionCN: 在 oxhide、ox tongue、ox-eye 等复合词中泛指牛
senses.example: The drum was stretched with oxhide.
senses.exampleCN: 这面鼓用牛皮蒙成。
senses.why: In compounds the sex distinction fades, and ox becomes a plain word for the animal's body or products.
senses.whyCN: 在复合词中性别区分淡化，ox 变成指动物身体或产物的普通词。

senses.title: Ox meat and parts
senses.definition: the meat or edible parts of an ox, as in ox tongue or ox cheek
senses.definitionCN: 阉牛的肉或可食部位，如牛舌、牛颊
senses.example: The ox tongue was boiled with herbs.
senses.exampleCN: 牛舌与香草一起煮。
senses.why: The working animal also enters the kitchen, and its name survives on cuts and dishes.
senses.whyCN: 役用动物也进入厨房，其名留在肉块与菜肴上。

senses.title: The zodiac Ox
senses.definition: the second sign of the Chinese zodiac, rendered in English as the Ox
senses.definitionCN: 中国生肖的第二位，英语译作 the Ox
senses.example: The Year of the Ox began with the new moon.
senses.exampleCN: 牛年随新月开始。
senses.why: Translation chose the farm ox as the English name for a zodiac branch, and the image stuck.
senses.whyCN: 翻译选用农家的牛作为某个生肖地支的英语名，这个意象固定下来。

senses.title: A very strong person
senses.definition: a person compared to an ox for strength or patient endurance
senses.definitionCN: 因力量或耐性而被比作牛的人
senses.example: He was strong as an ox and just as silent.
senses.exampleCN: 他力大如牛，也一样沉默。
senses.why: The ox's strength and patience, not its intellect, supply the comparison.
senses.whyCN: 提供比较的是牛的力气与耐性，而非智力。

senses.title: A yoke as a pair
senses.definition: a pair of oxen joined by one yoke, treated as a working unit
senses.definitionCN: 由同一副轭连成一对、作为一个劳作单位的牛
senses.example: A yoke of oxen could plough an acre in a day.
senses.exampleCN: 一对同轭耕牛一天能犁一英亩。
senses.why: The harness, not the animal, becomes the unit, and English counts ploughing by the yoke.
senses.whyCN: 成为单位的是轭具而非动物，英语按「轭」计算犁地。

senses.title: A sacrificial animal
senses.definition: an ox offered in classical or biblical sacrifice
senses.definitionCN: 在古典或圣经祭祀中献上的牛
senses.example: The temple accepted a perfect ox without blemish.
senses.exampleCN: 神庙接受一头无瑕的牛。
senses.why: The ox was the costliest common sacrificial animal, which is why the word appears in ritual law.
senses.whyCN: 牛是最昂贵的常见祭牲，因此这个词出现在祭祀律法中。

intro.en: Ox goes back to Old English oxa, from Proto-Germanic uhsō(n), from an Indo-European word for ox or bull. The plural oxen preserves an old strong ending. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ox 可上溯到古英语 oxa，来自原始日耳曼语 uhsō(n)，再上溯一个表示牛或公牛的印欧词。复数 oxen 保留古老强变化词尾。年代均为约数。

items.en: Oxa named the castrated male bovine, and the plural oxan already showed the old ending.
items.cn: oxa 指阉割的雄性牛，复数 oxan 已显示古老词尾。

items.en: The Germanic form is reconstructed from English, German and Old Norse evidence.
items.cn: 这个日耳曼形式是由英语、德语与古诺斯语证据重构的。

items.en: The root behind ox is a separate bovine word from the root that gives Latin bos and Greek bous, so the two families are not close relatives.
items.cn: ox 背后的词根与给出拉丁 bos、希腊 bous 的词根属于不同的「牛」词，因此两个词族并非近亲。

items.en: The plural oxen keeps a strong noun ending that most English nouns have lost, which is why the form looks irregular.
items.cn: 复数 oxen 保留多数英语名词已丢失的强变化词尾，因此这个形式看起来不规则。

items.en: The animal's role as a plough team and as a sacrifice gave English the phrases a yoke of oxen and the sacrificial ox.
items.cn: 这种动物作为犁队与祭牲的角色，给英语留下「一轭牛」与「祭牛」的说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the Indo-European form is reconstructed, and its relation to the other bovine roots is not settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：印欧形式属重构，它与其他「牛」词根的关系尚未定论。

note.en: Group one holds ox compounds that are easily mistaken for the animal; group two holds the separate words for bovine age, sex and use.
note.cn: 第一组是由 ox 构成、易被误当成动物本身的复合词；第二组是按年龄、性别与用途区分牛的独立词。

entries.definition: The U-shaped collar of an ox yoke, or a river bend of that shape; it is not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 牛轭的 U 形弯木，或形似它的河湾；它不是动物。

entries.definition: A daisy-like flower with a large yellow centre, named for its ox-eye look; it is a plant.
entries.definitionCN: 花盘大而黄、形似牛眼的花；它是植物。

entries.definition: A cart pulled by oxen; it names the vehicle, not the team.
entries.definitionCN: 由牛拉的车；它命名车辆，不是牛队。

entries.definition: A person who tends oxen; it is the keeper, not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 照看牛的人；它是看守者，不是动物。

entries.definition: An adult uncastrated male bovine; an ox is a bull that has been castrated for work.
entries.definitionCN: 成年未阉割的公牛；ox 是已为劳作而阉割的公牛。

entries.definition: A young castrated male bovine, often raised for beef; ox is usually older and trained to work.
entries.definitionCN: 年轻的阉公牛，常为肉用；ox 通常更年长且受训劳作。

entries.definition: A young bull or a castrated bull, especially in British regional use; it overlaps with ox but is usually younger.
entries.definitionCN: 年轻公牛或阉公牛，尤见于英国方言；与 ox 重叠，但通常更年轻。

entries.definition: Bovines as a group; ox names one castrated working animal within the herd.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的牛；ox 指牛群中一头阉割的役用牛。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English oxa and the old plural oxan explain the irregular oxen.
normal.cn: 古英语 oxa 与旧复数 oxan 解释了不规则的 oxen。

normal.en: The family runs ox, oxen, oxherd, oxcart, oxbow, oxhide, oxeye.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ox、oxen、oxherd、oxcart、oxbow、oxhide、oxeye。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the uses: a yoke of oxen, ox cart, ox hide.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分用法：一对同轭牛、牛车、牛皮。

normal.en: Ox is a castrated bull, not any bull; the knife made it workable.
normal.cn: ox 是阉过的公牛，不是任何公牛；是刀使它可用。

normal.en: The zodiac Ox is a translation choice, not a biological category.
normal.cn: 生肖牛是翻译选择，不是生物学类别。

abstract.en: Picture two heavy bodies joined by one wooden bar, moving as a single machine.
abstract.cn: 想象两具沉重的身体被一根木杠连成一台机器。

abstract.en: Picture a river bending back on itself like a yoke left in the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河弯回自身，像遗在草里的牛轭。

abstract.en: Picture a silent man carrying what four others cannot lift.
abstract.cn: 想象一个沉默的人扛起四个人抬不动的东西。

examples.en: A yoke of oxen pulled the stone boat.
examples.cn: 一对同轭耕牛拉着石船。

examples.en: The oxen were fed before the people.
examples.cn: 先喂牛，再喂人。

examples.en: He was strong as an ox but slow to anger.
examples.cn: 他力大如牛，却不易发怒。

dict_mnemonic.text: ox 是阉过的成年公牛，复数 oxen；套上轭就是耕牛，因此有 a yoke of oxen；牛皮、牛舌、牛眼菊都用它作限定成分。

root: 古英语 oxa「阉公牛」→ 原始日耳曼 uhsō(n) → 印欧牛词；复数 oxen 保留古强变化词尾。该词根与拉丁 bos、希腊 bous 不同源，更早形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one working animal: the castrated male, the draught team, the generic bovine, meat, the zodiac, strength, the yoke as a unit and the sacrifice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一头役用动物展开：阉公牛、役畜队、泛指牛、牛肉、生肖、力气、以轭为单位与祭牲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy animal stands under a wooden yoke, and the yoke turns it into a unit of power.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头沉重的动物站在木轭下，木轭把它变成一单位动力。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: castration defines the class before any work begins.
branches.cn: 动物：在开始任何劳作之前，阉割先定义了等级。

branches.en: THE TEAM: the pair under one yoke is the ploughing unit.
branches.cn: 牛队：同轭的一对是犁地单位。

branches.en: THE BODY: in compounds and in the kitchen, ox becomes plain bovine flesh.
branches.cn: 身体：在复合词与厨房里，ox 变成普通的牛肉与牛身。

branches.en: THE ZODIAC: translation turns the farm animal into a calendar sign.
branches.cn: 生肖：翻译把农场动物变成历法符号。

branches.en: STRENGTH AND SACRIFICE: the same body is admired for power and offered in ritual.
branches.cn: 力气与祭祀：同一具身体既因力量被赞叹，也在仪式中被献上。

intro.en: Ox is a native Germanic noun with an old irregular plural; its family is built by compounding, not by Latin suffixes.
intro.cn: ox 是日耳曼本族名词，带一个古老的不规则复数；其词族靠复合而非拉丁后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin relative exists for ox, since Latin bos and Greek bous belong to a different bovine root, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: ox 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因为拉丁 bos 与希腊 bous 属于另一「牛」词根，所以拉丁部分留空。

items.example: The Old English noun already meant the working animal.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语名词已指役用动物。

items.example: The ending survives only in a few nouns such as oxen.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾只保留在少数名词中，如 oxen。

items.structure: ox (English noun, from Old English oxa)
items.example: The ox pulled the cart without complaint.
items.exampleCN: 这头牛毫无怨言地拉车。

items.example: The oxen were yoked before dawn.
The oxherd slept beside the stall.
The oxcart carried the harvest home.

items.meaning: a yoke's U-shaped collar; a river bend
items.example: The river left an oxbow in the meadow.
items.exampleCN: 河在草地上留下一个牛轭弯。

items.example: The shield was covered with oxhide.

definition_zh: 使氧化；氧化（使某物与氧结合或失去电子）；生锈
definition_en: to make a substance combine with oxygen or lose electrons, or to undergo this change
core_image: 铁钉躺在漏雨的棚板下，几周后表面浮起一层橘红薄壳，用手一搓就掉粉
scene: 铁钉在潮湿的棚子里放了几周，表面起了一层橘红薄壳。Damp air will oxidize the nails within weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 oxidize 指使金属与氧结合、表面生成氧化物（第 1 个义项：使与氧结合）；句意：潮湿空气会让这些钉子几周内氧化。图中可辨识物件：铁钉、锈壳、漏雨的棚顶、接雨的盆。

pos.zh: 使氧化；使与氧结合；使失去电子

derivatives.zh: 由 oxidize 加动作名词词尾构成，义为「氧化过程」
由 oxidize 加已然词尾构成，义为「已氧化的」
由 oxidize 加进行词尾构成，义为「有氧化能力的」
由 oxidize 加施动词尾构成，义为「氧化剂」

senses.title: Make a substance combine with oxygen
senses.definition: to cause a substance to combine with oxygen and form an oxide
senses.definitionCN: 使物质与氧结合并形成氧化物
senses.example: Damp air will oxidize the nails within weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 潮湿空气会让这些钉子几周内氧化。
senses.why: The verb is the working form of the oxygen-based name: an agent, or the air itself, brings the gas into combination.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是以氧命名的那个词的动作形式：某个作用者，或者空气本身，促使这种气体与物质结合。

senses.title: Strip electrons from something
senses.definition: to remove electrons from an atom, ion or molecule, raising its oxidation state
senses.definitionCN: 从原子、离子或分子中移走电子，使其氧化态升高
senses.example: The reagent oxidizes the alcohol to an aldehyde.
senses.exampleCN: 该试剂把醇氧化成醛。
senses.why: Once oxidation meant any loss of electrons, the verb took on the transitive reading of forcing that loss on something.
senses.whyCN: 当氧化泛指任何失电子之后，这个动词就带上「迫使某物失电子」的及物含义。

senses.title: Rust or tarnish on its own
senses.definition: to undergo slow surface corrosion in air, without a named agent
senses.definitionCN: 在空气中缓慢发生表面腐蚀，不点明作用者
senses.example: Silver oxidizes quickly in air that contains sulfur compounds.
senses.exampleCN: 银在含硫化合物的空气中很快氧化变暗。
senses.why: Everyday observation has no experimenter, only a metal and the weather, so the verb commonly appears without an agent.
senses.whyCN: 日常观察里没有实验者，只有金属与天气，因此这个动词常以不带作用者的形式出现。

senses.title: Food or drink turning stale
senses.definition: to spoil through contact with air, as fats, wine or cut fruit do
senses.definitionCN: 因接触空气而败坏，如脂肪、葡萄酒或切开的水果
senses.example: Left uncovered, the wine oxidizes and loses its freshness.
senses.exampleCN: 敞着不放，葡萄酒会氧化并失去新鲜感。
senses.why: The kitchen applies the verb to flavours rather than surfaces, but the cause is the same combination with oxygen.
senses.whyCN: 厨房把这个动词用在味道而不是表面，但成因仍是同一种与氧的结合。

senses.title: Break down fuel in the body
senses.definition: to convert fats, sugars or other nutrients into smaller units with the help of oxygen in cells
senses.definitionCN: 在细胞中借助氧把脂肪、糖等营养物转成更小单位
senses.example: Muscles oxidize glucose during long exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间运动时肌肉会氧化葡萄糖。
senses.why: Physiology treats the reaction as the body's way of extracting energy, so the verb can name what cells do to fuel.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把这一反应视为身体提取能量的方式，因此这个动词可以指细胞对燃料所做的事。

senses.title: Raise an element to a higher valence
senses.titleCN: 把元素氧化到更高价态
senses.definition: to convert an element into a compound in which it has a higher oxidation number
senses.definitionCN: 使某元素转成氧化数更高的化合物
senses.example: The process oxidizes sulfur dioxide into the trioxide.
senses.exampleCN: 该过程把二氧化硫氧化成三氧化硫。
senses.why: In chemical writing the verb marks a direction on the number scale rather than the visible decay of a surface.
senses.whyCN: 在化学写作里，这个动词标出数字尺度上的方向，而不是表面的可见衰败。

senses.title: Grow a protective oxide layer
senses.definition: to form a thin oxide film on a surface on purpose, so that further damage is slowed
senses.definitionCN: 有意在表面生成薄氧化膜，从而减缓进一步损坏
senses.example: Engineers oxidize the aluminium panel to harden its skin.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师对铝板作氧化处理，使其表层变硬。
senses.why: The same reaction is turned to advantage: the crust that ruins iron can, on another metal, seal the surface.
senses.whyCN: 同一反应被转为有利：毁掉铁的那层壳，换到另一种金属上却能封住表面。

senses.title: Bleach or deactivate by oxidation
senses.definition: to use oxidation to remove colour or to destroy an unwanted substance
senses.definitionCN: 利用氧化去除颜色或破坏不需要的物质
senses.example: The mill oxidizes the dye so that the cloth comes out pale.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把染料氧化，使布匹变浅。
senses.why: Here the electron loss is valued for its side effect: colour and unwanted compounds are broken down rather than the metal being consumed.
senses.whyCN: 这里的失电子看重的是副作用：被拆掉的是颜色与不需要的化合物，而不是金属被消耗。

intro.en: Oxidize is built on oxide, itself from oxygen, the French scientific name of 1777; the verb's first date is approximate.
intro.cn: oxidize 由 oxide 派生，而 oxide 又出自 oxygen 这一 1777 年的法语科学命名；该动词的首见年代为约数。

items.en: The name of oxygen joins Greek oxys 'sharp, acid' with -genes 'producing', because Lavoisier believed the gas was required for acids.
items.cn: 氧的名称把希腊语 oxys「尖锐、酸」与 -genes「产生」合在一起，因为拉瓦锡相信酸的形成需要这种气体。

items.en: Lavoisier's new name spread through European science, and English adopted it at the end of the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 拉瓦锡的新名称在欧洲科学界传开，英语于 18 世纪末采用。

items.en: A compound of an element with oxygen was called an oxide, formed on the model of the new gas name with a chemical noun ending.
items.cn: 元素与氧形成的化合物被称为 oxide，是按新气体名称配上化学名词词尾构成的。

items.en: Oxidize was built directly on oxide with the ordinary verb ending that means 'to make or become', parallel to many other chemical verbs.
items.cn: oxidize 直接在 oxide 上加表示「使成为、变成」的普通动词词尾构成，与许多其他化学动词同型。

items.en: As chemistry, medicine and industry expanded, the verb was applied to metals, food, fuels, dyes and living tissue, and the noun oxidation followed the same range.
items.cn: 随着化学、医学与工业扩张，这个动词被用于金属、食物、燃料、染料与活组织，名词 oxidation 也覆盖同样的范围。

items.en: First date uncertain: the verb is recorded from the turn of the nineteenth century, but the earliest citations for the wider electron sense belong to later decades and are not precisely fixed.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：该动词在 19 世纪之交已有记录，但更宽的失电子义的最早引文要晚数十年，具体年份并未精确固定。

note.en: The first group shares the oxygen stem and differs by word class; the second group holds the paired or neighbouring changes in the same reaction.
note.cn: 第一组共享由氧派生的词干而词类不同；第二组是同一反应中与之配对或相邻的变化。

entries.definition: The event itself; the verb names what an agent does, while the noun names what happens.
entries.definitionCN: 事件本身；动词命名作用者所做的事，名词命名所发生的事。

entries.definition: The compound left behind; it cannot take an object and describes no change in progress.
entries.definitionCN: 留下的化合物；它不能带宾语，也不描述进行中的变化。

entries.definition: A participle or adjective for matter that has already changed, not for the act of changing it.
entries.definitionCN: 表示已经变化的物质的分词或形容词，而不是使其变化的动作。

entries.definition: The substance that accepts electrons and drives the change; in everyday writing oxidizer is the more common twin.
entries.definitionCN: 接受电子并推动变化的物质；日常写作中更常见的是 oxidizer 这一同义形式。

entries.definition: To add electrons or lower an oxidation number; every oxidation is balanced by a reduction somewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 加上电子或降低氧化数；每一处氧化都在别处由还原平衡。

entries.definition: To wear a metal away by chemical action; it describes the damage rather than the electron transfer.
entries.definitionCN: 借化学作用磨损金属；它描述损坏，而非电子转移。

entries.definition: To dull or discolour a metal surface, especially silver; it is a visible result of oxidation, not its general name.
entries.definitionCN: 使金属表面失去光泽或变色，尤指银；它是氧化的可见结果，而非其通称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: oxide plus the verb ending: to turn something into an oxide.
normal.cn: oxide 加动词词尾：把某物变成氧化物。

normal.en: The family runs oxide, oxidize, oxidation, oxidized, oxidizing, oxidizer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 oxide、oxidize、oxidation、oxidized、oxidizing、oxidizer。

normal.en: Typical objects: oxidize a metal, oxidize fats, oxidize the surface.
normal.cn: 典型宾语：使金属氧化、使脂肪氧化、氧化表面。

normal.en: Air does it slowly, a reagent does it fast, a cell does it for energy.
normal.cn: 空气做得慢，试剂做得快，细胞则为了取能而做。

normal.en: The same verb can ruin a nail or protect an aluminium panel.
normal.cn: 同一个动词既能让钉子报废，也能保护铝板。

abstract.en: Picture a slice of apple browning on a plate before anyone touches it.
abstract.cn: 想象一片苹果摆在盘子里，没人碰就先变褐。

abstract.en: Picture a silver spoon going grey in the drawer where it is never used.
abstract.cn: 想象一把银勺在抽屉里久不使用，慢慢变灰。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed bottle that slowly loses its sparkle because air got in.
abstract.cn: 想象一瓶密封饮料因为进了空气，慢慢失去气泡感。

examples.en: Heat and light oxidize the pigment, so the sign fades.
examples.cn: 热与光会氧化颜料，于是标牌褪色。

examples.en: The alloy oxidizes more slowly than pure iron.
examples.cn: 这种合金比纯铁氧化得慢。

examples.en: Bacteria oxidize the sulfides in the sediment.
examples.cn: 细菌氧化沉积物中的硫化物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oxi（氧）+ dize（使）」——让氧上身，就是使氧化

root: 英语 oxide（出自 oxygen，1777 年法语科学命名，取自希腊语 oxys「尖锐、酸」+ -genes「产生」）+ 动词词尾。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one transfer of electrons: oxygen joins, charge leaves, a surface rusts, food spoils, cells burn fuel, an element climbs in valence, a protective film grows, and a dye is bleached away.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次电子转移：氧结合进来、电荷离开、表面生锈、食物变陈、细胞烧燃料、元素价态上升、保护膜生成、染料被漂掉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nail under a leaking roof, its bright skin turning into a soft orange powder.
core.cn: 核心意象：漏雨棚下的铁钉，亮皮变成松软的橘色粉末。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY READING: air alone makes a metal combine with oxygen, and the result is plain rust or tarnish.
branches.cn: 日常读法：仅靠空气就让金属与氧结合，结果就是直白的锈或暗斑。

branches.en: THE CHEMIST'S READING: electrons are pushed out and an element is driven to a higher valence.
branches.cn: 化学家的读法：电子被推走，某元素被推上更高的价态。

branches.en: THE KITCHEN COST: air attacks a flavour instead of a surface, and the change is tasted rather than seen.
branches.cn: 厨房的代价：空气攻击的是味道而非表面，变化靠尝而非靠看。

branches.en: THE ENERGY USE: cells oxidize fuel on purpose because the transfer releases power.
branches.cn: 能量的用法：细胞有意氧化燃料，因为这一转移能放出能量。

branches.en: THE INDUSTRIAL TWIST: the same reaction is made to seal a panel or to strip colour from cloth.
branches.cn: 工业的转折：同一反应被用来封住板材，或被用来剥去布上的颜色。

intro.en: Oxidize is a stem from the name of oxygen with a verb ending, and the family keeps that stem in every form.
intro.cn: oxidize 是以氧的名称作词干、再加动词词尾构成，整个词族在各种形式里都保留这个词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Greek and passed through French scientific naming; Latin supplies only the endings, so no Latin root relative is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词干源自希腊语并经法语科学命名传入；拉丁语只提供词尾，因此不列出该词根的拉丁同族词。

items.example: The opening element points to the acid-making claim.
items.exampleCN: 开头的成分指向「产酸」这一说法。

items.example: The suffix says the gas produces the quality named first.
items.exampleCN: 后缀说明这种气体产生前面所指的性质。

items.structure: oxygen stem plus a chemical noun ending
items.example: The oxide film dulls the metal.

items.structure: oxidize plus the action noun ending
items.example: Oxidation is faster in wet air.
The oxidized surface no longer shines.
items.exampleCN: 已氧化的表面不再发亮。

items.example: Nitric acid is a strong oxidizing agent.

items.meaningCN: 使其他物质氧化的物质
items.example: The fuel needs an oxidizer to burn in space.
items.exampleCN: 燃料在太空燃烧需要氧化剂。

derivatives.zh: 由 oxidize 加动作名词词尾构成，义为「氧化过程」
由 oxidize 加已然词尾构成，义为「已氧化的」
由 oxidize 加进行词尾构成，义为「有氧化能力的」
由 oxidize 加施动词尾构成，义为「氧化剂」

definition_zh: 氧；氧气；空气中的氧；供呼吸用的氧气
definition_en: the chemical element that makes up about a fifth of the air, is needed for breathing and burning, and is supplied in cylinders for medical or high-altitude use
core_image: 看不见的气体让火苗忽然蹿高一截
scene: 清晨的树林里，叶子在阳光下无声地工作。By midday the leaves had released enough oxygen into the clearing for a walker to feel the air turn fresh.
sceneCN: 这里要说明的是氧这种气体（第 1 个义项：空气中支持呼吸与燃烧的那种元素）；句意为到正午时，树叶已经把足够的气体释放到林间空地上，让散步的人觉得空气变清新了。图中可辨识物件：树叶、阳光、林间小路。

senses.title: The element that makes up part of the air
senses.definition: the chemical element that forms about a fifth of the air and is needed for breathing and for burning
senses.definitionCN: 组成空气约五分之一的化学元素，呼吸和燃烧都离不开它
senses.example: Green plants give off oxygen during the day.
senses.exampleCN: 绿色植物在白天释放氧气。
senses.why: Greek oxys means sharp or sour and -genes means born or producing; the gas was named for the acids it was once thought to create.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 oxys 意为尖锐、酸，-genes 意为产生；人们曾以为这种气体能生成酸，命名就从此而来。

senses.title: A supply of the gas for breathing
senses.definition: the gas supplied in cylinders or through a mask so that people can breathe where the air is thin or unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 装在钢瓶里或经面罩供给的氧，用于空气稀薄或不宜呼吸的地方
senses.example: Climbers above eight thousand metres often breathe bottled oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 八千米以上的登山者常常吸瓶装氧。
senses.why: As soon as oxygen names the gas itself, it can also name the measured amount of it that a hospital ward or a climber carries along.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 oxygen 指这种气体本身，也就能指医院病房或登山者随身携带的那一份定量供氧。

senses.title: The active part of air in burning and rusting
senses.titleCN: 氧（引起燃烧与生锈的成分）
senses.definition: the element thought of as the substance in air that combines with other materials when something burns or rusts
senses.definitionCN: 指空气里在燃烧或生锈时与其他物质结合的那种成分
senses.example: Oxygen in the damp air slowly turned the iron gate red with rust.
senses.exampleCN: 潮湿空气里的氧慢慢把铁门锈成了红色。
senses.why: Because the same gas makes a flame leap and makes iron decay, the word also names the partner hidden inside those two very different changes.
senses.whyCN: 因为同一种气体既能让火苗蹿起，也能让铁慢慢朽坏，所以这个词也指藏在这两种截然不同的变化背后的那一方。

intro.en: Oxygen is a scientific coinage of the late eighteenth century: two Greek roots were joined in French and then borrowed into English.
intro.cn: oxygen 是十八世纪后期造出的科学术语：两个希腊词根在法语里拼合，随后被英语借用。

items.en: Oxys meant sharp or sour, and the suffix -genes meant born or producing; together they described something that generates acid.
items.cn: oxys 意为尖锐、酸的，后缀 -genes 意为产生；两者合起来描述「能生成酸的东西」。

items.en: The French chemist Lavoisier and his colleagues are generally thought to have coined oxygène for the part of air they believed produced acids in combustion.
items.cn: 一般认为法国化学家拉瓦锡与同事造出 oxygène 一词，用来指他们所认为的、在燃烧中生成酸的那部分空气。

items.en: English adopted the French term as oxygen, and it quickly replaced the older vocabulary of phlogiston in chemical writing.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪九十年代借入法语术语，写作 oxygen，并很快在化学著作中取代了旧的燃素说法。

items.en: As chemistry settled, oxygen became the name of a single element, and compounds such as oxide and dioxide fixed the ox- stem.
items.cn: 随着化学体系定型，oxygen 成为一个元素的名称，oxide、dioxide 这类化合物词也固定了 ox- 这个词干。

items.en: Modern English uses oxygen for the gas in air, for bottled supplies in hospitals and aircraft, and loosely for anything a situation cannot do without.
items.cn: 现代英语里，oxygen 指空气中的氧、医院与飞机上的瓶装氧，也松散地指任何缺了就撑不下去的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the other element names built with the same Greek ending; the near-meaning group gathers words for the air and for what we breathe.
note.cn: 形近组收其他用同一个希腊词尾构成的元素名；近义组收表示空气与呼吸的词。

entries.definition: The lightest element, named from Greek for water and the same -genes ending.
entries.definitionCN: 最轻的元素，由希腊语「水」加同一个 -genes 词尾构成。

entries.definition: The element that makes up most of the air, named from a root meaning soda.
entries.definitionCN: 占空气大部分的元素，名称来自表示碱的词根。

entries.definition: A compound in which oxygen is joined to another element.
entries.definitionCN: 氧与另一种元素结合形成的化合物。

entries.definition: A compound containing two atoms of oxygen in each molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 每个分子含两个氧原子的化合物。

entries.definition: The mixture of gases around us that we breathe.
entries.definitionCN: 我们周围可以呼吸的混合气体。

entries.definition: The layer of gases surrounding a planet.
entries.definitionCN: 包围一颗行星的气体层。

entries.definition: The air taken into and sent out of the lungs.
entries.definitionCN: 吸入与呼出肺部的空气。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Greek-rooted scientific label, and its whole family keeps the same two ideas: air and the making of acids or oxides.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是希腊词根造出的科学名称，整族词都围绕两个念头：空气，以及酸或氧化物的生成。

normal.en: Greek oxys means sharp or sour and -genes means producing, so the name literally says acid maker.
normal.cn: 希腊语 oxys 是尖锐、酸的，-genes 是产生，所以这个名字字面上就是「造酸者」。

normal.en: Oxygen takes about a fifth of the air by volume, while nitrogen takes most of the rest.
normal.cn: 按体积算，氧约占空气的五分之一，其余大部分是氮。

normal.en: Oxide and dioxide keep the ox- stem, and the ending -ide marks a compound of two elements.
normal.cn: oxide 与 dioxide 保留 ox- 词干，-ide 后缀表示两种元素组成的化合物。

normal.en: Oxidize and oxygenate are both verbs built on the same stem, one about combining with oxygen, the other about supplying it.
normal.cn: oxidize 与 oxygenate 都是同一词干上的动词，一个指与氧化合，一个指供给氧。

normal.en: An oxygen mask is simply the word turned into an object that fits over the face.
normal.cn: oxygen mask 只是把这个词变成一件罩在脸上的器物。

abstract.en: The gas that keeps a flame alive is also the gas that quietly eats iron, so the same power both feeds and destroys.
abstract.cn: 让火焰活下去的气体，也会悄悄吃掉铁；同一种力量既供养也销毁。

abstract.en: The name was built on a mistake about acids, yet it outlived the theory that produced it.
abstract.cn: 这个名字建立在关于酸的误解之上，却比产生它的理论活得更久。

abstract.en: Oxygen is invisible, and every breath is the moment it becomes visible as a need.
abstract.cn: 氧是看不见的，而每一次呼吸都是它作为「需要」显形的时刻。

examples.en: Green plants give off oxygen during the day.
examples.cn: 绿色植物在白天释放氧气。

examples.en: Climbers above eight thousand metres often breathe bottled oxygen.
examples.cn: 八千米以上的登山者常常吸瓶装氧。

examples.en: Oxygen in the damp air slowly turned the iron gate red with rust.
examples.cn: 潮湿空气里的氧慢慢把铁门锈成了红色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥克斯精」——听成「奥克斯精华」，深吸一口，记住 oxygen 是氧。

root: 希腊语 oxys（尖锐、酸）加 -genes（产生），十八世纪法语据此造出 oxygène，再进入英语；同族词有 oxide、dioxide、oxidize。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the gas in the air that keeps breath and flame going; the senses then divide into the element itself, a bottled supply, and the active partner in burning and rust.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是空气里维持呼吸与火焰的那种气体；义项由此分为元素本身、瓶装供应，以及燃烧与生锈时参与反应的那一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gas nobody can see, making a flame jump and a breath come easier.
core.cn: 核心意象：一种谁也看不见的气体，让火苗蹿高，也让呼吸顺畅。

branches.en: a leaf exchanging gas with the air at noon
branches.cn: 正午一片叶子与空气交换气体

branches.en: a candle burning brighter when fresh air moves in
branches.cn: 新鲜空气流入时蜡烛烧得更旺

branches.en: a climber breathing from a cylinder near the summit
branches.cn: 登山者在山顶附近吸钢瓶里的氧

branches.en: an iron gate turning red in wet weather
branches.cn: 铁门在潮湿天气里泛红

branches.en: a hospital bed with a mask resting on the pillow
branches.cn: 病床上搁着一只面罩

intro.en: The word is a modern scientific compound of two Greek pieces, and English suffixes then build the chemistry around it.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个希腊部件拼成的现代科学复合词，英语后缀随后在它周围建起一整套化学词汇。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; the term was coined in French from Greek roots, and the later scientific Latin form oxygenium is a modern borrowing of that coinage.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；术语是用法语从希腊词根造出的，后来科学拉丁语里的 oxygenium 只是对这一新造词的借用。

definition_zh: 打包；背包；一包
definition_en: to put things in a bag, a bag on the back, or a set sold together

sceneCN: 这里的 pad 是「便笺本」（第 2 个义项：一叠可撕的纸）；句意为她把地址写在电话旁的便笺本上。图中可辨识物件：便笺本、撕开的纸边、笔。

senses.title: A soft piece used for protection or comfort
senses.definition: a piece of soft material placed under or against something to protect it, soften it or make it more comfortable
senses.definitionCN: 垫在某物下面或贴着某物的柔软材料，用来保护、缓冲或增加舒适
senses.example: The chair needs a new pad on the seat.
senses.exampleCN: 这把椅子的座面上需要一块新衬垫。
senses.why: Pad first named a soft bundle used as a bed or a cushion, so the word starts with something yielding placed under the body rather than with any shape.
senses.whyCN: pad 最初指当作床铺或坐垫的软捆，所以这个词的起点是垫在身体下面的一块软东西，而不是某个形状。

senses.title: A block of paper for writing
senses.definition: a number of sheets of paper glued together along one edge so that they can be torn off one by one
senses.definitionCN: 把若干张纸沿一边粘在一起，可以一张张撕下来使用
senses.example: She wrote the address on a pad by the telephone.
senses.exampleCN: 她把地址写在电话旁的便笺本上。
senses.why: A writing pad is a flat block of sheets, and that flat soft block looks exactly like the cushion the word already named, so one word covered both.
senses.whyCN: 便笺本是一叠压平的纸，而这个平整柔软的块状物，看起来正像这个词早先指的坐垫，于是一个词兼指两样东西。

senses.title: To stuff or line with soft material
senses.definition: to fill or cover something with soft material so that it is protected, fuller or more comfortable
senses.definitionCN: 用柔软材料把某物填满或包住，使它受到保护、更饱满或更舒适
senses.example: They padded the box with newspaper before posting it.
senses.exampleCN: 寄出之前，他们用报纸把箱子填塞好。
senses.why: The verb turns the cushion into an action: to pad something is to put a pad inside it, and from packing a box the sense spread to padding a speech with extra words.
senses.whyCN: 动词把坐垫变成动作：给某物加衬，就是往里面塞垫料；从给箱子填塞出发，这个意思又扩展到用多余的话把发言拉长。

senses.title: To walk quietly with soft steps
senses.definition: to walk with soft, quiet steps, especially with bare feet or paws
senses.definitionCN: 脚步轻软、几乎没有声响地走，尤指赤脚或动物用肉垫行走
senses.example: He padded across the room in bare feet.
senses.exampleCN: 他赤着脚轻轻走过房间。
senses.why: Bare feet or an animal's soft paw lands without a sound, and the word for a soft cushion became the verb for a walk that sounds like one.
senses.whyCN: 赤脚或动物的软掌落地几乎没有声响，于是「软垫」这个词又变成动词，指一种听上去像踩在垫子上的走法。

intro.en: The origin of pad is uncertain; the cushion sense is recorded in the sixteenth century, and one common suggestion links it to a Low German or Dutch word for the sole of the foot, but no origin is settled.
intro.cn: pad 的来源不确定；坐垫义在十六世纪已有记录，一种常见的推测把它联系到低地德语或荷兰语中表示脚掌的词，但没有定论。

items.en: The noun pad for a cushion appears in the sixteenth century, and dictionaries disagree about its source; a Low German or Dutch word for the sole of the foot is often suggested.
items.cn: 表示坐垫的名词 pad 在十六世纪出现，各词典对它的来源说法不一，常有人推测与低地德语或荷兰语中表示脚掌的词有关。

items.en: Pad named a soft bundle, a straw bed and a cushion, and it was also used for the stuffed saddle of a horse.
items.cn: pad 指软捆、草铺与坐垫，也曾用来指马背上加软垫的鞍。

items.en: The noun widened to any soft guard worn on the body, and the verb appeared with the sense of stuffing something with soft material.
items.cn: 词义扩展到身上穿的任何软护具，动词也随之出现，表示往某物里塞软材料。

items.en: A pad of paper named a block of sheets glued at one edge, and the verb gained the sense of walking with soft, quiet steps.
items.cn: a pad of paper 指沿一边粘住的一叠纸；动词也获得了脚步轻软地走这一义。

items.en: Modern English adds notepad, mouse pad and launch pad, keeps padding for stuffing material, and uses pad out for filling a text with needless matter.
items.cn: 现代英语加上 notepad、mouse pad 与 launch pad，保留 padding 表示填充物，也用 pad out 指用多余内容把文字拉长。

normalIntro.en: Pad is a short word for something soft and flat, and its hooks follow that flatness from a cushion to a block of paper and to a quiet footfall.
normalIntro.cn: pad 是一个表示「软而平的东西」的短词，记忆钩子顺着这份平整，从坐垫走到一叠纸，再走到一声轻软的脚步。

normal.en: Pad doubles its final consonant before a suffix, so the forms are padded and padding rather than paded.
normal.cn: pad 在加后缀前要双写末尾的辅音，所以形式是 padded 与 padding，而不是 paded。

normal.en: A pad of paper and a shoulder pad share one idea: a flat soft block that sits against something.
normal.cn: 一叠便笺纸与一块肩垫共有一个想法：一块平软的垫状物贴着别的东西。

normal.en: Padlock has nothing to do with a cushion, so the two words only look alike and must not be confused.
normal.cn: padlock 与坐垫毫无关系，两个词只是长得像，不能混为一谈。

normal.en: To pad a speech is to stuff it, exactly as a box is stuffed with paper before posting.
normal.cn: 给发言注水就是往里塞东西，和寄包裹前往箱子里塞纸一模一样。

normal.en: Pad across and pad along describe bare feet or soft paws, never the sound of heavy boots.
normal.cn: pad across 与 pad along 描写的都是赤脚或柔软的脚掌，绝不是沉重靴子的声响。

abstract.en: A word that means both a cushion and a notebook suggests that comfort and record-keeping can rest on the same flat softness.
abstract.cn: 一个词既指坐垫又指便笺本，说明舒适与记录可以建立在同一种平软之物上。

abstract.en: Padding protects a fragile thing and also makes it look bigger, which is why the same idea describes a parcel and a bloated essay.
abstract.cn: 填充既保护易碎之物，也让它显得更大，所以同一个概念既能说包裹，也能说一篇注水的文章。

abstract.en: Walking padded is walking as if the floor were a cushion, and the word quietly turns the ground into something kind.
abstract.cn: 轻步走就像把地板当成一块软垫，这个词悄悄把地面变成了温和的东西。
